$comment: SPEC §6.3 / §34.4 — namespaced error-code enum. Prefixes are the closed namespace set AUTH_/ASTRO_/VOICE_/PAY_/SAFE_/SYS_. HTTP status follows the §6.3 convention: 400 validation · 401/403 auth · 402 entitlement · 409 conflict/idempotency · 422 domain rule · 429 rate · 5xx system. New codes are PR-reviewed like analytics events (taxonomy owner: backend lead, W2). This is the M0 seed, not the full taxonomy.

members.$comment: §33.1 — the original recording expired, was deleted per-note, or was never stored (ephemeral voice-input mode). Gone, and deliberately so: the transcript remains and the bubble shows a 'voice input' marker.

§30.3's S33 — expired, already redeemed, or no such code. ONE code for all three on purpose: a caller that could tell 'expired' from 'never existed' is an oracle for guessing gift codes, and §30.3 gives all three the same warm error and support link anyway.

No payment provider is IMPLEMENTED for this billing region. Distinct from PAY_PROVIDER_ERROR, which means a wired rail answered badly: this means none is wired. Today it is what a real Razorpay/Stripe region returns while `payments.providers.routing` still has them DECLARED — the gap made a runtime state rather than a silent fallback to the simulator.
§22.16 — the 7-day no-questions window is annual-only and has passed. Not a 403: the caller is entitled to ask, and the answer is about the policy rather than about them.
